newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Continental to start up Brazil flights at discount.
newsitem.headline: Continental to start up Brazil flights at discount.

text.p: U.S. carrier Continental Airlines Inc is starting up its daily flights from Brazil to Newark International Airport near New York July 11 with an introductory offer of $814 for a round-trip flight, a senior airline official said.

Continental Vice-President for Latin American and Caribbean sales Ralph Schulz said the new route from Rio de Janeiro via Sao Paulo to Newark marked the airlines entrance into the largest Latin American market with the best growth potential.
As of September, Continental will be serving Rio de Janeiro and Sao Paulo with two separate direct flights to Newark.

"We expect double digit growth in air travel over the next five years," Schulz told reporters in Rio de Janeiro. "Given the improvements in the Brazilian economy and growth in air travel Brazil is expected to grow 15 to 20 percent over a five-year period."

Schulz said the introductory air fare represented a 25 percent reduction on current price levels and remained valid until December 9 for tickets purchased before July 15. The flights to and from Brazil will use DC-10 planes.

Continental is investing $100 million in the new route, which will increase to 32 the number of destinations the carrier flies to in Latin America and the Caribbean, plus $1 million to provide Portuguese and Spanish speaking staff at U.S. airports.
Brazil Country Manager Giovanni Luigi said Continental was also looking into a code-sharing agreement with a local airline and may announce one in the near future.
Continental is the United States' fifth largest carrier with revenues of $6.3 billion in 1996, and 40 percent of the company's growth this year is expected to be generated in Latin America.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
